method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley) 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases' (published 16 September 2025), 27 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC12439324). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from EULAR task force (Fanouriakis A, Kostopoulou M, Andersen J, et al.), Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases 2024;83:15-29 (doi 10.1136/ard-2023-224762) 'EULAR recommendations for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus: 2023 update' (published online 12 October 2023), 10 claims; LICENCE: © Author(s) (or their employer(s)) 2024. No commercial re-use. See rights and permissions. Published by BMJ. (read at copyright line on page 1 of the published PDF (University of Szeged repository copy of the BMJ version)). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 adds S2, the EULAR 2023 SLE recommendations (published BMJ PDF from the University of Szeged repository, pdftotext; the same text used by `cutaneous-lupus-erythematosus`), paraphrased and hash-anchored. The S1 claims and anchors are unchanged from edition 1.0. Table rows appended with pmc_text.py --append-tables (2026-09-24); claims from S1 Tables 1 (Australia/NZ differences), 2 (pregnancy) and A2 (supportive care). S1 Tables 3, A1, A3, A4 and A5 were not extracted (no header row or merged cells).

claims.claim: **Report kidney biopsies with a validated international scoring system** (for lupus nephritis, the ISN/RPS classification). Biopsy remains key in glomerular disease when the cause is not clear.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **With marked proteinuria in adults, prefer a timed urine collection** over a random spot sample to measure protein: it is more accurate and varies less.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Creatinine-based eGFR overestimates true GFR** in nephrotic syndrome with low albumin, and CKD-EPI is unvalidated in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander and Māori people.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Give people starting immunosuppression a third primary COVID vaccine dose** (ATAGI), ideally more than 2 weeks before treatment starts. This covers high-dose steroids (> 20 mg/day for > 14 days), mycophenolate, azathioprine, calcineurin inhibitors, cyclophosphamide and anti-CD20 agents.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Australian and NZ adjustments to KDIGO (CARI):** depending on the setting, serology or genetic tests may stand in for, or accompany, a kidney biopsy; and for patients under 25, CARI backs the 2021 CKiD U25 eGFR equation. For ANCA vasculitis, CARI endorses KDIGO unchanged.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not wait for a biopsy or positive serology before treating AAV,** especially when kidney function is falling fast.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not base treatment decisions on ANCA titres alone:** positivity or rising titres do not reliably predict relapse. Loss of PR3-ANCA after rituximab goes with longer remission; turning from negative to positive goes with higher relapse risk.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Induce remission with a glucocorticoid plus cyclophosphamide or rituximab.** Prefer rituximab in children and adolescents, pre-menopausal women, men worried about fertility, older adults, relapsing disease and PR3-ANCA positive disease.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **With severe disease (serum creatinine > 354 μmol/L), prefer glucocorticoid plus cyclophosphamide.** IV cyclophosphamide suits a moderate cumulative dose, low white cell count or poor adherence, where an infusion centre is close.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Give pneumocystis prophylaxis for the whole cyclophosphamide course, or for 6 months after rituximab,** and monitor IgG for hypogammaglobulinaemia.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use reduced-dose steroids:** with cyclophosphamide, bring prednisolone down to 5 mg/day within 6 months; with rituximab, stop it within 6 months. **Avacopan** can spare or replace glucocorticoids and has been PBS-listed for ANCA vasculitis since October 2024.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Reserve plasma exchange for specific cases:** diffuse alveolar haemorrhage, creatinine > 5.7 mg/dL (500 μmol/L) needing dialysis, rapidly rising creatinine, or combined AAV and anti-GBM disease.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In anti-GBM plus ANCA double-positive disease, maintain as for ANCA vasculitis.**
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Proteinuria does not reliably track how severe the nephritis is,** so assess clinical and laboratory findings together. Base the decision to treat class III/IV disease on the biopsy.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hydroxychloroquine for every patient.** First-line induction is a corticosteroid with a mycophenolic acid analogue (MPAA) or low-dose IV cyclophosphamide, starting with IV glucocorticoid pulses then a lower starting dose tapered quickly.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Choose between MPAA and low-dose cyclophosphamide on availability, adherence, age, severity, ethnicity and past treatment:** efficacy is similar and low-dose cyclophosphamide has fewer adverse events. Standard-dose IV cyclophosphamide may help severe disease (AKI, cellular crescents, fibrinoid necrosis).
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Alternatives:** MPAA with a calcineurin inhibitor. ⚠️ Belimumab (for lupus nephritis) and voclosporin (which helps when eGFR > 45 mL/min/1.73 m2, with MPAA) are **not available in Australia or New Zealand**.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Maintain with low-dose glucocorticoid plus MPAA;** azathioprine is second line, then a calcineurin inhibitor or mizoribine. Continue for at least 36 months, stopping glucocorticoids after 12 months in complete remission.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Rituximab is an option for refractory disease or when steroids must be minimised.** Class V treatment depends on proteinuria, with RAAS blockade plus immunosuppression for nephrotic syndrome.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **EULAR: for active proliferative lupus nephritis, give low-dose (Euro-Lupus) IV cyclophosphamide or mycophenolate with glucocorticoids (IV methylprednisolone pulses, then lower oral doses), and consider adding belimumab or a calcineurin inhibitor (voclosporin or tacrolimus with mycophenolate) from the start.** The add-on is left to the treating doctor; if it is not used first, add belimumab or voclosporin when response is inadequate at 3–6 months.
claims.locator: EULAR task force (Fanouriakis A, Kostopoulou M, Andersen J, et al.), Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases 2024;83:15-29 (doi 10.1136/ard-2023-224762), 'EULAR recommendations for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus: 2023 update', published online 12 October 2023, http://publicatio.bibl.u-szeged.hu/28452/3/34193576_megjelent.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Choosing the add-on (EULAR):** belimumab worked better when baseline proteinuria was under 3 g/day; voclosporin lowers proteinuria quickly, which may suit nephrotic-range disease, but its safety at GFR 30–45 mL/min is unknown because AURORA-1 excluded GFR below 45. In the small pure class V subgroups, neither beat placebo on renal response.
claims.locator: EULAR task force (Fanouriakis A, Kostopoulou M, Andersen J, et al.), Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases 2024;83:15-29 (doi 10.1136/ard-2023-224762), 'EULAR recommendations for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus: 2023 update', published online 12 October 2023, http://publicatio.bibl.u-szeged.hu/28452/3/34193576_megjelent.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Class V (EULAR): the proteinuria threshold for starting immunosuppression is 1 g/day,** unchanged from the 2019 EULAR/ERA-EDTA advice.
claims.locator: EULAR task force (Fanouriakis A, Kostopoulou M, Andersen J, et al.), Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases 2024;83:15-29 (doi 10.1136/ard-2023-224762), 'EULAR recommendations for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus: 2023 update', published online 12 October 2023, http://publicatio.bibl.u-szeged.hu/28452/3/34193576_megjelent.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Patients at high risk of kidney failure** (reduced GFR, cellular crescents, fibrinoid necrosis or severe interstitial inflammation) can have high-dose (NIH) IV cyclophosphamide, 0.5–0.75 g/m2 once a month for 6 months, with IV methylprednisolone pulses. Such patients were under-represented or excluded in the recent trials.
claims.locator: EULAR task force (Fanouriakis A, Kostopoulou M, Andersen J, et al.), Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases 2024;83:15-29 (doi 10.1136/ard-2023-224762), 'EULAR recommendations for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus: 2023 update', published online 12 October 2023, http://publicatio.bibl.u-szeged.hu/28452/3/34193576_megjelent.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Response targets (EULAR/ERA-EDTA 2019, now validated):** proteinuria down by at least 25% at 3 months and 50% at 6 months, and under 500–700 mg a day by month 12, with GFR staying within 10% of baseline.
claims.locator: EULAR task force (Fanouriakis A, Kostopoulou M, Andersen J, et al.), Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases 2024;83:15-29 (doi 10.1136/ard-2023-224762), 'EULAR recommendations for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus: 2023 update', published online 12 October 2023, http://publicatio.bibl.u-szeged.hu/28452/3/34193576_megjelent.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **EULAR maintenance:** keep treating for at least 3 years after response. Stay on a mycophenolate-based regimen (with belimumab or a calcineurin inhibitor if those were used); after cyclophosphamide, switch to mycophenolate or azathioprine and keep belimumab if it was part of the first regimen.
claims.locator: EULAR task force (Fanouriakis A, Kostopoulou M, Andersen J, et al.), Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases 2024;83:15-29 (doi 10.1136/ard-2023-224762), 'EULAR recommendations for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus: 2023 update', published online 12 October 2023, http://publicatio.bibl.u-szeged.hu/28452/3/34193576_megjelent.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **In sustained remission, taper gradually, stopping glucocorticoids first.** In the WIN-LUPUS trial, withdrawing mycophenolate or azathioprine after 2–3 years of lupus nephritis treatment was not shown to be non-inferior: those who stopped had more renal relapses and extra-renal flares.
claims.locator: EULAR task force (Fanouriakis A, Kostopoulou M, Andersen J, et al.), Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases 2024;83:15-29 (doi 10.1136/ard-2023-224762), 'EULAR recommendations for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus: 2023 update', published online 12 October 2023, http://publicatio.bibl.u-szeged.hu/28452/3/34193576_megjelent.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Before conception:** discuss the risks to the mother, the baby and the kidney disease; avoid teratogenic drugs (renin–angiotensin system inhibitors, most immunosuppressants) or use safe contraception while taking them; and weigh the total cyclophosphamide dose, as it can leave permanent infertility.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **During pregnancy:** care from a team of nephrologist, obstetrician and maternal–fetal medicine specialist. Do not use RAS blockers or certain immunosuppressants, for example mycophenolate. Consider low-dose aspirin with calcium and vitamin D, aim for blood pressure under 140/90 mmHg, and consider prophylactic anticoagulation (heparin or a heparin derivative preferred) at high thrombosis risk: nephrotic syndrome, earlier VTE, high BMI.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **After the birth:** bring in a paediatric nephrologist if the baby may have an inherited kidney disease, and a pharmacist if the mother wants to breastfeed on drugs that reach breast milk. Rarely, antibody-mediated disease (such as FSGS or membranous nephropathy) crosses the placenta.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Lifestyle:** sodium below 2 g (90 mmol) a day; moderate, preferably plant-based, protein restriction; carbohydrate no more than 35 kcal/kg of ideal body weight, and fewer calories with a high BMI; a heart-healthy diet, reaching ideal weight, more exercise, stopping smoking and less alcohol.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Blood pressure: aim for systolic under 120 mmHg** using RAAS blockade, plus further blood-pressure drugs as needed.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oedema:** start with a loop diuretic, add a thiazide if needed, and consider amiloride or spironolactone when loop diuretics fail. **Lipids:** a statin when cardiovascular risk is high, as with diabetes or hypertension.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Prophylactic anticoagulation:** decide on histology, amount of proteinuria and serum albumin, helped by an online bleeding-risk tool; heparin, a heparin derivative or warfarin is preferred, and direct oral anticoagulants have not been studied.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Infection:** every patient gets pneumococcal and influenza vaccines and screening for TB, syphilis, hepatitis and HIV; high-dose steroids or other immunosuppression call for pneumocystis prophylaxis.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hydroxychloroquine for every patient unless contraindicated, aiming at 5 mg/kg of actual body weight a day,** adjusted to flare and retinal-toxicity risk. A higher start (not above 400 mg/day) can be used in moderate or severe disease, then lowered. Kidney disease raises retinal risk, so eye follow-up should be closer.
claims.locator: EULAR task force (Fanouriakis A, Kostopoulou M, Andersen J, et al.), Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases 2024;83:15-29 (doi 10.1136/ard-2023-224762), 'EULAR recommendations for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus: 2023 update', published online 12 October 2023, http://publicatio.bibl.u-szeged.hu/28452/3/34193576_megjelent.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Glucocorticoids: dose by organ and severity, taper to 5 mg/day or less (prednisone-equivalent) for maintenance, and stop when possible.** In moderate-to-severe disease, IV methylprednisolone pulses of 125–1000 mg a day for 1–3 days can be used. The maintenance ceiling was lowered from 7.5 mg/day in 2019.
claims.locator: EULAR task force (Fanouriakis A, Kostopoulou M, Andersen J, et al.), Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases 2024;83:15-29 (doi 10.1136/ard-2023-224762), 'EULAR recommendations for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus: 2023 update', published online 12 October 2023, http://publicatio.bibl.u-szeged.hu/28452/3/34193576_megjelent.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **If SLE does not respond to hydroxychloroquine (with or without steroids), or steroids cannot be cut to an acceptable long-term dose, add an immunosuppressant (methotrexate, azathioprine or mycophenolate) and/or a biologic (belimumab or anifrolumab).** EULAR sets no order between the two biologics, and a conventional immunosuppressant need not be tried first.
claims.locator: EULAR task force (Fanouriakis A, Kostopoulou M, Andersen J, et al.), Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases 2024;83:15-29 (doi 10.1136/ard-2023-224762), 'EULAR recommendations for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus: 2023 update', published online 12 October 2023, http://publicatio.bibl.u-szeged.hu/28452/3/34193576_megjelent.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24
